newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia to probe logging costs.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia to probe logging costs.

text.p: British Columbia said on Monday it was launching a study into wood and logging costs in the province after complaints from forest companies.
British Columbia forest companies have said that government regulations and bureacracy had pushed up their costs to uncompetitive levels and strangled the flow of wood.

Research will begin by the end of January with a preliminary report due within four weeks. Forests Minister David Zirnhelt said the government might ultimately look at policy changes to reduce costs and increase jobs.

The government said the study would analyze the coast and interior regions of the province separately. It is being jointly sponsored by the industry, and forest companies will open their books to the study team.
Financial records for all major forest license holders will be examined and chief executives of forest companies will provide input.
